outputs.explanation: Main panel is a scatter plot where each marker is one of the n = 141 individual sample measurements (rhythmicity index vs. period), i.e., the points themselves are the raw data. The marginal histograms show the distribution of these same raw values (with a fitted gamma curve), not group averages requiring point overlay.

Each plotted point represents an aggregated mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter (per caption). This is an average/summary statistic (mean with error bars), but the underlying individual replicate measurements are not shown on the plot.

Panel shows fitted normal-distribution density curves (line plots) of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes. Overlaying individual points on continuous density curves is not practical and this plot type is exempt from the check.

Boxplots inherently display data distribution (quartiles, median, whiskers, outliers) and are exempt from requiring separate individual data point overlays; the panel additionally already shows scattered per-sample dots within the boxes.

Polar histograms display the (probability-normalized) distribution of phase differences over time per cell line; like standard histograms, the bars themselves represent the underlying data distribution, so individual point overlay is not required.
Polar histogram of subtype-averaged phase differences; as a distribution/histogram-type plot it is exempt from needing individual data point overlays.
This panel is an illustrative example of a single signal trace with a fitted decaying sinusoid, not a summary/average plot across samples, so the individual-data-points check does not apply.

Scatter plot where each of the n = 117 points is an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for that single sample rather than variability across pooled replicates, so the points already are the individual data (exempt scatter-plot type).
